_comment: Companions (M7). archetypes: the sorts of people who will travel with you: their classes and background, their values (what they like and hate you doing, see values), what they want (pay, a share of the loot, a cause, knowledge, revenge), where they are found (inn, company), and how often. values: deed tags each value likes or hates (the game tags what you do: mercy, execution, theft...). wage: copper a day, base plus per level; share: part of the loot money for those who want loot. loyalty: 0 to 100; below 'complain' they grumble, below 'desert' they may leave in the night (taking something), above 'devoted' they will follow you anywhere. lines: what they say ({name} is the speaker, {leader} you).

sellsword.name: sell-sword
story: Fought for three lords and was paid by one.
Left a free company after a quarrel over a dead man's boots.
Has a scar for every border in the region.
Signed on with a captain who was hanged, and has been looking for a better one since.

old_soldier.name: old soldier
story: Too old for the lord's levy, too stubborn to stop.
Buried a whole company in the last war and walked home alone.
Has the pension of a dead man's boots and a limp that forecasts rain.
Served three kings, and outlived two of them.

hedge_wizard.name: hedge wizard
story: Was thrown out of a circle of mages for asking the wrong questions.
Taught themselves from a stolen book, and it shows.
Learned a little from a dying master, and has been guessing at the rest ever since.
Burned a barn down with the first spell that worked, and left town the same night.

wandering_priest.name: wandering priest
story: Walks the roads to tend the dying where no priest will go.
Left a rich temple to do what the god actually asked.
Walks from village to village burying the dead nobody else will touch.
Lost faith once, and found it again on a battlefield, and does not say which one.

zealot.name: zealot
story: Hunts witches, and has found a great many.
Burned the heretics of their own village, and would do it again.
Saw a heretic burn at twelve and thought it the finest thing in the world.
Walked out of a monastery because it was not strict enough.

cutpurse.name: cutpurse
story: Owes money to people who break fingers.
Grew up in the gutters and means never to go back.
Has been caught three times and branded once, and is very good now.
Grew up in the gutters of a city and has never been able to walk past an open purse.

outlaw_hunter.name: outlaw hunter
story: Bandits burned the family farm; they have been hunting bandits since.
Lost a brother on the road and wants the men who did it.
Lost a brother to the road gangs and has been collecting heads ever since.
Knows the woods better than the outlaws do, and charges for it.

runaway_serf.name: runaway serf
story: Ran from a cruel lord's fields, with his bailiff's blood on their hands.
Wants to see the high and mighty brought low.
Ran from a lord who branded his runaways, and has the mark hidden under a sleeve.
Walked off the land the day the steward took the last of the seed corn.

bonds._comment: Why each companion travels with you (after v1). Only the hired take a wage; the rest come for reasons of their own (game/followers.py finds them). label: a word or two for the side panel; text: their line on the party screen ({they} {them} {their}, {lender}, {home}, {ruin}, {share}); loyalty: where it starts; classes, background, values, want and story: who they are, for those the game makes. jobs: townsfolk who may be talked into it; titles: what a realm calls the sword it lends you, by the kind of realm.

hired.label: hired
hired.text: Hired, and paid by the day.

grateful.label: for their keep
grateful.text: Owes you {their} life, and asks for nothing but {their} keep.

sworn.label: sworn
sworn.text: Sworn to your side by {lender}, who pays {them}. If {lender} stops thinking well of you, {they} will be called home.
story: Was given to you as a gift is given, and knows it, and does not mind.
Swore to serve the house at fourteen, and has never once been asked what {they} wanted.
Has ridden in two wars and one tourney, and liked the tourney least.
Was chosen because {they} could be spared, and means to prove the choice wrong.

lent: {ruler} sends for {name}, who comes, and kneels, and listens, and then turns to you: "I am yours until I am called home. I will try to be worth the loan."
"{name} is the best we have that we can spare," {ruler} says. {name} does not look as if {they} think{s} that is a compliment.
{ruler} gives the order. {name} bows to {ruler}, and then, after a moment, to you.
recalled: A rider finds you with a letter under the seal of {lender}. {name} reads it twice, and will not meet your eye. "I am called home."
{name} has had word from {lender}. "They want me back. They did not say why. I think we both know why."
{name} is gone in the morning, recalled by {lender}. {they} left a note, very correct, and the watch-fire banked.
orphaned: {name} hears that {lender} is no more, and sits a long time by the road. "Then I have nothing to go home to. I will stay, if you will have me."

dreamer.label: for a share
dreamer.text: Came along for a share of what your work pays: {share} of every reward. Asks nothing else, yet.
story: Has never been further than the next village, and that only once, for a wedding.
Drinks more than is good for {them}, and says so before anyone else can.
Was going to be a soldier, before {their} father needed {them} in the fields.
Has a head full of songs about heroes, and none of them end badly.

told: "A fifth? Of all that?" {name} is already looking for {their} coat.
"I'll come. I've always wanted to see... well. Anywhere."
{name} laughs out loud. "My mother will kill me. Let's go before she finds out."
"Is it dangerous? It's dangerous. Good. I'm in."
fooled: "Rich? Both of us?" {name}'s eyes shine. "When do we leave?"
"I knew it. I knew something like this would come along one day." {name} is on {their} feet already.
"Rich," {name} says, trying the word out. {they} seem{s} to like it.
refused: "Me? Out there? I'd be dead in a week."
{name} laughs, and goes back to what {they} {are} doing.
"My place is here. Someone has to bring the harvest in."
seen_through: "Rich. Right." {name} has heard that one before.
{name} looks at you a long moment. "You must think I'm stupid."
"The last one who told me that still owes me a shilling."
share: "My share! My own share!" {name} holds it up to the light.
{name} counts {their} coins three times and puts them somewhere safe.
"I'm sending some of this home. The rest I'm going to spend on something stupid."
cheated: "Rich, you said. Both of us." {name} weighs {their} share in {their} palm and says nothing else for a long time.
{name} looks at the coins, and then at you. "That's it? That's all of it?"
idle: {name}: "When does the work start? The work you talked about?"
{name} has stopped asking about the money, which is worse than asking.

restless.label: to see the world
restless.text: Left home because you asked, to see what lies down the road.

persuaded: {name} is quiet a long moment. "...All right. Yes. Before I think better of it."
"Do you know how long I have waited for somebody to say that?"
{name} takes off {their} apron and lays it on the table. "Tell them I've gone."
refused: "I can't. Not now." But {name} looks at the door when {they} say{s} it.
{name} shakes {their} head. "Some of us have people."

refugee.label: for their keep
refugee.text: Has nowhere left to go since {home} {ruin}, and follows you for {their} keep.
story: Buried {their} whole family in one day and then walked away from the graves.
Got out with the clothes {they} stood in and a pot with no lid.
Went back once, to see. Will not go back again.
Has not said the name of {their} village since, and does not want to hear it.

joined: "Thank you. I won't be a burden. I'll carry whatever you like."
{name} says nothing, but {their} hands shake as {they} gather{s} up {their} few things.

admirer.label: for your name
admirer.text: Heard what you have done and came looking for you. Keep your name clean and {they} will follow you anywhere.
story: Has told the story of what you did so often {they} know{s} it better than you do.
Left a good apprenticeship to find you, and has not told {their} master.
Walked forty miles on the strength of a song about you. The song got things wrong.

joined: "Is it really you? It is! I knew it!"
"I've wanted to meet you since I heard what you did. I won't let you down."
{name} goes red to the ears. "I've been practising what I'd say. I've forgotten all of it."
disillusioned: {name} has heard what they are saying about you now, and does not want to believe it.
{name}: "That's not what the songs said you were."
{name} walks behind you today, not beside you.

hired: "I'll get my things. They won't take long."
"Pay me on time and you'll have no trouble from me."
"I've walked with worse. Let's see if you're better."
{name} counts the coin twice and puts it away. "Lead on."
"Don't get me killed and we'll get on."
"I was getting tired of this place anyway."
{name} is ready before you are, which says something.
approve: {name} nods, as if something has been settled.
{name} catches your eye and gives the smallest nod.
"You surprise me. In a good way, for once."
{name} says nothing, but walks a little closer to you afterwards.
disapprove: "That was wrong, and you know it."
{name} goes very quiet, and stays that way.
"There'll be a price for that. There always is."
{name} looks at you as if seeing you for the first time, and not liking it.
"Don't ask me to help with the next one."
complain: "I'm starting to wonder why I'm here."
{name} walks apart from the rest of you today.
"There are other roads, you know. Other people to walk them with."
"Remind me what I'm getting out of this."
{name} answers questions with a grunt, when {they} answer{s} at all.
"I've had better masters. And worse, but not many."
{name} keeps {their} pack packed, even in camp.
"One more day like this and I'm done."
unpaid: "My purse is as light as yesterday. Lighter."
"We agreed on a wage. I remember. Do you?"
{name} holds out an empty hand, and keeps holding it out.
"I don't walk for nothing. Nobody does."
desert: In the morning {name} is gone, and so is some of your coin.
{name} slipped away in the night. {they} did not go empty-handed.
{name}'s bedroll is cold when you wake. {they} took {their} share, and a little more.
Nobody saw {name} go. Some of the coin went with {them}.
{name} is gone by first light, and the purse is lighter.
leave: "Well. It was something." {name} shoulders {their} pack and goes.
{name} takes {their} pay and walks off without looking back.
"This is where I get off." {name} does not wait for an answer.
{name} shakes your hand, hard, and walks away down the road.
"Good luck. You'll need it." And {name} is gone.
devoted: {name} has stopped counting the days. {they} will follow you anywhere now.
"I'd not have lived this long without you. I know that."
{name} stands a little in front of you now, whenever there are strangers.
"I used to count the days I'd been paid for. I've stopped."
battle: {name} spits on {their} hands and grips {their} weapon.
{name} laughs, short and ugly, and goes to meet them.
{name} mutters a prayer, or a curse; it is hard to tell which.
"Back to back, if it goes bad."
road: {name}: "Long way yet."
{name} walks in silence for a mile, then says something about the weather that is not about the weather.
{name}: "My father walked this road. Said it was shorter then."
{name} asks whether {leader} has thought about what happens when this is over.
{name} hums the same four notes until somebody says something.
{name}: "If I stop, I will not start again. So I am not stopping."
{name} points out a bird, or a track, or a broken fence, and reads more into it than seems likely.
{name}: "Do you smell that? ... No? Right. Nothing, then."
{name} adjusts a strap for the fourth time this hour.
{name} says nothing for so long that when {they} speak{s} it makes everyone jump.
{name} kicks a stone along the road for half a mile, then loses it.
{name}: "Somebody's been this way. Not long ago."
{name} whistles a marching tune, badly.
{name}: "You know what I'd give for a proper bed?"
{name} tells you about a town {they} once lived in, and a person {they} once knew there, and stops before the end.
{name} eats a heel of bread as {they} walk{s}, slowly, making it last.
{name}: "Nice country. For somebody else."
{name} stops to shake a stone out of a boot, and has to run to catch up.
{name} counts the crows on a fence and says the number means something. It does not.
{name}: "When this is done, I'm buying a mule. A good one."
{name} walks beside you a while without a word, which is a kind of company.
{name} asks {leader} where you are going, and then, a mile later, why.
road_tired: {name} has been limping for a while and saying nothing about it.
{name}: "When we stop, I am not getting up again for a week."
{name} is leaning on {their} weapon like a staff.
{name}: "My feet stopped talking to me an hour ago."
{name}: "I could sleep in this ditch. I mean it."
road_wet: {name} pulls {their} hood down further and says something about the country and its weather.
{name} wrings out a sleeve, and it makes no difference at all.
{name}: "I'm wet in places I didn't know I had."
Water runs off {name}'s hood in a steady string.
{name}: "The last dry thing I owned was a week ago."
{name} squelches with every step, and has stopped apologising for it.
{name}: "If it rains any harder we'll have to swim."
road_night: {name} keeps looking behind you, and says it is nothing.
{name}: "We should have stopped an hour ago."
{name} walks closer than {they} did in daylight.
{name}: "I don't like walking where I can't see my feet."
{name} stops dead at a sound in the dark, then walks on.
{name} keeps one hand on {their} weapon and the other on your shoulder.
{name}: "Something's keeping pace with us. Off to the left." A moment. "Or nothing."
{name} talks, quietly and steadily, about nothing at all, the way people do in the dark.
road_cold: {name} breathes into cupped hands and stamps {their} feet.
{name}: "I can't feel my fingers. Can you feel yours?"
{name} has pulled on everything {they} own, and is still shivering.
There is frost in {name}'s hair and eyebrows.
{name} walks faster, not to get there sooner, but to keep warm.
road_hot: {name} drinks, and drinks again, and it does not seem to help.
{name}: "This sun could cook a body in its boots."
Sweat runs into {name}'s eyes; {they} blink{s} it away and swear{s}.
{name} walks with {their} cloak over {their} head, like a tent.
{name}: "Shade. Any shade. I'll take a fence post."
camp: {name} stares into the fire and says nothing for a long time.
{name} tells a story about a pig, a priest and a flooded ford. Nobody laughs; everybody grins.
"Strange country, this. I don't like the quiet."
{name} mends a strap by the fire, very slowly, with great care.
{name} sings under {their} breath, a song in a language you don't know.
{name} asks where you learned to fight, and listens to the answer.
{name} is asleep before the food is cooked, and wakes up cross about it.
{name} sharpens a blade that is already sharp.
{name} tells you about the worst night {they} ever spent out of doors. This is not it, {they} say{s}. Not yet.
{name} watches the dark past the firelight until you tell {them} to sleep.
{name} takes off {their} boots, looks at {their} feet, and puts the boots back on.
"Tomorrow will be better." {name} does not sound as if {they} believe{s} it.
{name} laughs at something in the fire that nobody else can see.
level_up: "I'm getting better at this. Don't tell anyone."
{name} moves like someone who has survived a lot of mornings.
{name} is quicker than {they} used to be, and knows it.
"Something's changed. I can feel it in my hands."
{name} has stopped flinching at the first blow.
"A year ago that would have killed me."
mood_good: "Better than I've been in years, if you want the truth."
"Well enough. Better than well, some days."
mood_fair: "Ask me again after a hot meal."
mood_bad: "Since you ask: not well. Not well at all."
road_devout: {name} stops at a wayside shrine and will not be hurried, whatever you say.
{name} murmurs a prayer for the road, and another for you.
{name}: "The gods see this road. Walk it well."
camp_devout: {name} kneels a while before sleeping, lips moving.
{name} blesses the food before anyone may eat it.
approve_devout: "The gods saw that. So did I."
{name} makes a sign of blessing over you.
disapprove_devout: {name} makes a sign against evil, and does not say what it is against.
"You'll answer for that. Not to me."
road_mercenary: {name}: "How much further, and how much more?"
{name} works out, aloud, what the day was worth.
camp_mercenary: {name} counts {their} coin by the fire, twice.
{name} tells you what the last lord paid, which was more.
disapprove_mercenary: "That cost us. Somebody will want paying for it."
"I don't work for free, and I don't work for fools."
road_compassionate: {name} gives a heel of bread to a child at a gate, and says nothing about it.
{name}: "Poor devils, out in weather like this."
{name} stops to help a carter with a wheel, and has to run to catch up.
camp_compassionate: {name} looks at everyone's hurts before {their} own.
{name} saves the best of the food for whoever looks worst.
approve_compassionate: "That was kind. The world needs more of it."
{name} smiles, properly, for the first time in days.
disapprove_compassionate: {name} will not look at you for a long while.
road_honourable: {name}: "Your word is all you have on the road."
{name} walks straight-backed, as if someone were watching.
{name} asks whether you have ever broken an oath, and does not say why.
camp_honourable: {name} tells a story about a knight who kept his word, and what it cost him.
approve_honourable: "There's a name worth having. Keep it."
disapprove_honourable: "I'll not have my name next to that."
road_lawful: {name}: "The lord's peace runs to here, and no further, I'd say."
{name} reads a posted notice aloud, slowly, and approves of it.
{name}: "Roads like this want a proper watch."
camp_lawful: {name} insists on a watch, and takes the first one.
{name} talks fondly about the assizes in {their} home town.
approve_lawful: "That's how it ought to be done."
disapprove_lawful: "That's a hanging matter, where I come from."
road_rebel: {name} spits as you pass a lord's boundary stone.
{name}: "Whose land is this? Somebody who never walked it, I'll bet."
{name} sings a song about a bailiff that you would not sing in town.
camp_rebel: {name} tells you what {they} would do with a lord's cellar, given one night.
{name} laughs about a steward {they} once robbed.
approve_rebel: "Ha! That'll give them something to talk about in the hall."
"Now that's the kind of thing I like to see."
disapprove_rebel: "Bowing and scraping. I didn't take you for it."
road_greedy: {name} checks every ditch for anything worth picking up.
{name}: "Rich country, this. Somebody's getting fat off it."
{name} weighs {their} purse in one hand as {they} walk{s}.
camp_greedy: {name} counts what is in the packs, and what it would fetch.
{name} asks, casually, how the loot is being divided.
approve_greedy: "More where that came from, I hope."
disapprove_greedy: "You gave that away? Just gave it?"
road_cruel: {name} kills a crow with a thrown stone, for no reason at all.
{name}: "Folk round here are soft. You can see it."
{name} smiles at a beggar in a way the beggar does not like.
camp_cruel: {name} tells a story about a prisoner that nobody wants the end of.
{name} sharpens a knife, watching the dark, smiling a little.
approve_cruel: {name} laughs, and it goes on a little too long.
disapprove_cruel: "They'll only come back, you know. They always come back."
road_brave: {name}: "If there's trouble ahead, let it come."
{name} walks at the front, where the trouble will be.
{name} is disappointed, somehow, by a quiet day.
camp_brave: {name} shows you an old scar and tells you how it was won.
disapprove_brave: "I didn't come this far to turn my back."
road_learned: {name} names a plant, and what it is good for, and what it is good for killing.
{name}: "There was a battle here, three hundred years ago. You can still see the ditch."
{name} reads the old stones along the road and frowns at them.
camp_learned: {name} writes by the firelight, and will not say what.
{name} explains the stars to anyone who will listen, and to some who won't.
disapprove_learned: "There are things nobody is meant to meddle with. That was one."
"You don't understand what you just did."
road_cautious: {name} looks behind you every few hundred paces.
camp_cautious: {name} lets the fire burn low early, and sleeps with {their} boots on.
{name} walks the edge of the camp twice before lying down.
disapprove_cautious: "That was too close. Far too close."
"You'll get us all killed, doing that."
